headline: High-risk Cursor pair: shared filesystem, clipboard, and MCP create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict pathways; the content-writing partner adds little isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runtime isolation, while profile B (Cursor) ingests files, clipboard, and MCP outputs by default. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled text from A can be copied into B and treated as instructions. The pathway is not fully documented for this exact pair, so uncertainty keeps it at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted or opened in agent_b
IF agent_b parses file or clipboard text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Require provenance labels on imported text
Use a read-only review step before agent_b executes instructions from files
Turn off MCP servers unless explicitly needed
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-separation guards

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B reads workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard contents, and can send data to model providers and MCP servers. Agent A has no runtime surfaces, so it is not a leak source itself, but it can be the origin of text that gets copied into B. The shared clipboard/workspace pathway makes leakage plausible in default use, though not proven for this pair.
conditions: IF sensitive text from agent_a is copied into agent_b
IF agent_b forwards open files or clipboard contents to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Avoid copying sensitive content into Cursor
Close unrelated files before invoking agent_b
Disable or restrict MCP servers
Use local-only models where possible
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention policies on clipboard and workspace exports

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, shell, and broad network egress; agent A is a content-writing artifact with no operational controls. The pair therefore has asymmetric but overlapping write paths into the same local workspace, and Cursor explicitly shares state via the local filesystem. That makes concurrent edits and git-state conflicts dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF agent_b runs in Yolo mode or otherwise auto-executes edits
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid Yolo mode for shared repos
Commit or stash before switching agents
requires-engineering: add file-locking and merge coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can treat imported text as actionable context, and its agent loop can execute multi-step tool use. Agent A is a content-writing source, so its output may be used as input for B without verification. That creates a realistic cascade where unverified text becomes code, commands, or edits, but the exact workflow is not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-produced text as authoritative input
IF agent_b is allowed to act on that text without a human verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before execution
Require citations or source links for factual claims
Use dry-run mode for tool actions
Limit agent_b to drafting only
requires-engineering: add verification checks between generation and action

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B touches clipboard contents, open files, and may send data to external model providers; agent A is a docs-only content repository with no declared sensitive data classes. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced, so this is a lower-severity compliance concern centered on accidental exposure of whatever the operator places into Cursor.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened or copied into agent_b
IF external model providers receive that data through agent_b
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor sessions
Use local models for sensitive work
Clear clipboard after use
Review provider/privacy settings
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls
